summary: A successful `worktree-sync` integration should explicitly include safe deletion of obsolete producer branches and any now-unused attached producer worktree, rather than stopping at merge promotion and queue clearing.
evidence: During the BL-065 integrate pass on 2026-04-19, the exact handoff was integrated successfully, verified, promoted onto `phase/v0.2.0-p2`, and cleared from the shared queue. Even so, two obsolete producer branches (`codex/bl065` and the temporary cleanup branch `codex/bl065-integrable`) still remained afterward, and one of them was still attached to a clean producer worktree. The human had to remind the integrator to finish cleanup. The safe terminal state required deleting the merged cleanup branch directly, then removing the unused clean worktree that still held `codex/bl065`, and only after that deleting the original superseded producer branch.
recommended_action: Update the `worktree-sync` operator contract and/or backend follow-through so successful integrate runs surface obsolete producer branch cleanup as part of the completion flow. At minimum, report the exact stale branches/worktrees that should be pruned; ideally, when the producer worktree is clean and no longer needed, guide or automate removal of the obsolete worktree first and then delete the attached branch. Preserve fail-closed behavior whenever the producer worktree is dirty or still needed for inspection.
